decisions.reason: The client confirms the Hero V is working and must remain preserved, which is already represented by its fixed-reference and unchanged-geometry requirements; no value or scope changes.
The source confirms the second V is working but does not alter its established height hierarchy or visual role; the same-message verification already records the execution result.
The literal copy-and-paste rule and its continued application are already entailed by the current exact-vector derivation requirement and project-persistent full-wordmark scope.
The source confirms the second V is working without changing its geometry, Hero-V derivation, or right-arm reach; the same-message verification already captures that result.
The source reiterates literal accent derivation but does not independently change the existing exact peak-alignment rule or its fixed Hero V reference.
Requiring the literal Hero V termination to persist is already represented by the shared exact-signature-gesture requirement; no terminal treatment attribute changes.
Presenting E and L concepts within complete wordmarks does not change the established kerning or unified-reading requirement.
The source concerns preservation of letterform relationships during E and L exploration and does not resume or modify the deferred champagne material treatment.
The instruction to build on approved decisions and evaluate one variable at a time does not change the separate obligation to provide a brief design rationale with each review round.
